structure: Independent persons follow a linear Gaussian scenario: Z, U and V are independent standard normals; X = 0.6Z + 0.8U; Y = 0.6Z + 0.8(0.25U + sqrt(1 - 0.25^2)V). This satisfies the supplied population moments and chooses an otherwise unspecified correlation between the population OLS residuals.

parameter_provenance.basis: All three population means are exactly zero.
All three individual population variances are exactly one; z_sd is therefore one.
Exact marginal Pearson correlations in the same population.
The intercept-adjusted population slope is correlation times outcome SD divided by Z SD; all SDs equal one.
Each population OLS residual variance is 1 - 0.6^2 = 0.64.
A freely chosen point scenario; neither record specifies the X-Y covariance.
A convenient joint distribution implementing the required moments and chosen residual correlation.

requested_estimands.name: partial_xy_given_z
requested_estimands.basis: For population OLS residuals, partial correlation = (r_XY - 0.6*0.6)/sqrt((1 - 0.6^2)(1 - 0.6^2)) = (r_XY - 0.36)/0.64. The records leave r_XY unspecified; the generator chooses residual correlation 0.25.

requested_estimands.name: marginal_xy
requested_estimands.basis: The selected residual correlation gives Cov(X,Y) = 0.36 + 0.8*0.8*0.25 = 0.52. Both variances equal one, so this is also the marginal Pearson correlation.

requested_estimands.name: slope_x_on_z
requested_estimands.basis: With an intercept, the population OLS slope is Cov(X,Z)/Var(Z) = 0.6. This follows from B and C without Gaussianity or any assumption about the X-Y relationship.

limitations: The records permit marginal X-Y correlations throughout [-0.28, 1] and OLS residual correlations throughout [-1, 1]; the two chosen scenario values are not identified.
Gaussianity is an implementation assumption, not evidence. It is unnecessary for the second-moment identities or the identified X-on-Z slope.
Reported constraints hold at the model-population level. Random finite samples will not have exactly zero means, unit variances or the target correlations, and the generator does not force them.
This is an artificial mathematical population, not a clinically validated or causal model.
checks_actually_performed: Analytically checked zero population means and variances Var(X) = Var(Y) = 0.36 + 0.64 = 1, with Var(Z) = 1.
Analytically checked Cov(X,Z) = Cov(Y,Z) = 0.6 and Cov(X,Y) = 0.52.
Analytically checked positive definiteness: the residual covariance matrix has diagonal 0.64 and off-diagonal 0.16, giving determinant 0.384; the full covariance matrix also has determinant 0.384.
Analytically checked that residual correlation is 0.16/0.64 = 0.25.
No code execution or empirical sample checks were performed.
